Presidential Gubernatorial The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has directed President Bola Tinubu’s campaign council in FCT to block opposition parties from securing 25 per cent of votes in the territory during the 16 January presidential election.
Mr Wike gave the charge while inaugurating the 466-member All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in FCT on Monday.
The minister specifically named the opposition parties as the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).
He said the campaign team’s mandate goes beyond a simple victory to achieving an overwhelming margin for President Tinubu and APC National Assembly candidates.
“We’re not talking about winning; we’re talking about winning overwhelmingly.
“We must not allow them to go with 25 per cent. They don’t deserve to get 25 per cent,” Mr Wike told the gathering, which included council members, party supporters, and members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).
Addressing claims by opposition figures regarding political dominance ahead of the 2027 polls, the minister dismissed assertions that the ADC held sway in northern states or stood a chance in the nation’s capital.

He singled out the ADC’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, noting his tenure as vice president from 1999 to 2007, and argued that past administrations failed to deliver foundational policy reforms for the FCT.
Mr Wike also challenged former Rivers governor, Rotimi Amaechi, whom he referenced in connection with opposition remarks about an APC rally in Port Harcourt, to test his party’s popularity in Rivers State.
“The FCT is for no other party other than the APC,” Wike, a member of the PDP, declared, warning council members that they would be held directly accountable for the election outcome in the territory.
To persuade voters, the minister urged the council to campaign on the current administration’s governance reforms and infrastructure record rather than mere promises.
According to him, the Tinubu administration has introduced historic structural changes since 2023, including appointing an FCT representative to the Federal Executive Council (FEC) for the first time since Abuja’s creation in 1976 and establishing dedicated Mandate Secretariats for Women and Youth.
He noted that the administration also created the FCT Civil Service Commission, appointed the first Head of Service for the FCT, and enabled career civil servants to rise to the rank of permanent secretary.
On financial autonomy and land administration, Mr Wike, a former governor of Rivers State, said the removal of the FCT from the Treasury Single Account (TSA) allowed direct access to financial markets for capital projects, leading to the signing of over 20,000 Certificates of Occupancy (C of O) within three years, compared to roughly 8,000 issued between 1999 and 2023.
He added that traditional rulers had been elevated, while road networks, police stations, and educational projects, such as the proposed University of Science and Technology in Abaji, were expanded across satellite towns and rural communities.
Wike commended the leadership of the APC and PDP in the FCT for setting aside party rivalries to form the Rainbow Coalition in support of the president’s re-election and National Assembly candidates.
He identified the candidates as Philip Aduda, seeking election to represent the FCT in the Senate, John Gabaya for AMAC/Bwari Federal Constituency and Danladi Chiya for Abuja South Federal Constituency.
He urged other states to emulate the alliance model practised in the FCT, Rivers and Akwa Ibom.
He instructed the council to establish local campaign committees across all FCT area councils and take their message directly to markets, suburbs, traditional rulers, indigenes, and non-indigene associations while maintaining peace and adherence to electoral laws.
In his remarks, the FCT Chairman of the APC, Ishaku Yamawo, commended the party leadership for fostering unity across political divides and specifically recognised members of the “Rambo Coalition,” a cross-party political structure associated with the FCT minister.
Mr Yamawo said the coalition’s willingness to work alongside the APC demonstrated that the party’s strength lay in building partnerships and pursuing a common political objective, adding that the developmental projects executed under Tinubu’s “Renewed Hope” agenda served as the party’s primary campaign message.
“The people can see the transformation taking place,” Mr Yamawo said.
He added that Mr Wike’s appointment as the coordinator of the FCT Presidential Campaign Council was a strategic decision based on his capacity for grassroots mobilisation.
He pledged that the territory’s party structure was fully mobilised to deliver votes for President Tinubu and all APC National Assembly candidates, urging members to remain disciplined and sustain the prevailing atmosphere of political cooperation across all wards and polling units.
Also speaking, the FCT Chairman of the PDP, Mohammed Dogara, praised Mr Wike for what he described as unbiased leadership that has united rival political camps in the capital territory.
Using a local proverb, Mr Dogara commended the minister for “bringing the cat and the rat to build the house and live in the house without any issues,” noting that such collaboration between APC and PDP leaders in the FCT was unprecedented.
Mr Dogara assured the minister that local council chairmen and grassroots leaders in the territory were fully capable of mobilising voters even in his absence.
He expressed optimism that the coalition’s efforts would secure victory at the polls on 16 January 2027, naming Messrs. Aduda, Gabaya and Chiya as beneficiaries of the unified political front.
“Come 17th of January, we are going to rejoice and celebrate the resounding victory,” he said.
